results.health: The tag core is in decent shape: image_tags is a genuine single owner, tag_names/tag_canon/tag_categories are small pure modules, and invalidation really is structural. The weak spots are structural: tag_index (786 lines) fuses cache primitives, cover pins, mosaic samples, browse, character classification and the 8-query detail panel; cover pins and focus (tag_meta/tag_focus) are written from five modules including the router; and 'is this tag a character' has two implementations that disagree. The image_tags/tag_index import cycle (broken by a lazy import) is also the shape problem the tag-weights write path will land in. Already-reported items touching this slice (find_image projection, id_candidates loops, bulk prompt write twin, clear_ai_all unbounded tx, deprecated POST /tags/ai, app_settings JSON helper copies) are not repeated.

findings.title: Renaming a source-specific tag moves the cover, focus and character settings of the shared base name
findings.problem: Pins, focus and `characters` rows are keyed by base name (`pin_key` strips the kind prefix). `_move_thumbnail` and `_move_character` run `pin_key` on both sides, so renaming only `manual:foo` to `manual:bar`, or writing a prompt rule `foo -> bar`, relocates the pinned cover, its framing and the whole `characters` row of base `foo` to `bar` even though the AI tag `foo` (or other sources) still exists and still owns that page. With a merge onto an existing target the old pin is simply deleted. A user who renames a manual duplicate of a character tag can lose the character page's avatar, colour and kind override.
findings.proposal: Only carry pin/focus/character state when no other source of the old base remains after the operation: add `_base_survives(conn, old_base)` (an EXISTS on `image_tags.base == old_base` excluding the tag being renamed) and skip `_move_thumbnail`/`_move_character` when true. Add a test in test_tag_rename_integration.py: AI tag `foo` pinned, rename `manual:foo` to `manual:bar`, assert the `foo` pin is untouched.
invariants_touched: pins belong to the tag name, not a source (CONTEXT: Tag index)

findings.title: Two diverging definitions of 'is a character': tag_rename._character_names vs tag_index._characters
findings.problem: The Tags page decides character-ness in `tag_index._characters` (listed names, plus bare-name candidates the library backs via `_listed_characters`, then `characters.kind` overrides, treating kind NULL as no override). The rename/split guard and merge-suggestions filter use `tag_rename._character_names`, which takes only `vocab.names`, ignores library-backed bare candidates (`furina`), and treats a kind-NULL `characters` row as a character (the else branch). So a bare-name character the Tags page shows as a character can still be split by a rule ('is a character, so it can't be split' is not raised), and suggestions are offered for it. CONTEXT.md says the library check lives in tag_index but the vocabulary concept belongs with tag_categories.
findings.proposal: Move `_characters`, `_listed_characters` and `_may_be_characters` out of tag_index into one `services/character_names.py` (or tag_categories) exposing `async def character_names(conn, vocab, bases: set[str] | None) -> frozenset[str]` (bases None = every library base, using the cheap candidate walk). tag_index._browse, tag_rename (`_write_rule`, `merge_suggestions`) and characters.py call it. Delete `tag_rename._character_names`. Decide the kind-NULL semantics once (tag_index's: no override).
invariants_touched: Tag category (CONTEXT)

findings.title: Split tag_index.py: cache primitives, cover pins, browse, character classification and the detail panel are fused
findings.problem: One 786-line module owns six jobs. `detail` alone is a 128-line function issuing 8 queries (span, kinds, months, loras, embeddings, sigs, related, pin) that repeats the same 'row's image is not quarantined' EXISTS that `image_ids` and `_listed_characters` also build. characters.py reaches into the private `tag_index._pins`. The tag-weights spread aggregate (plan step 4) would add a ninth query to `detail`.
findings.proposal: Keep tag_index.py as the cache owner only (invalidate, generation, read/store view/derived, ~90 lines, imported by writers). Move: (1) `pin_key`, `_pins`, `_seed*`, `_shuffled`, `samples_for_tag` to `tag_covers.py` (public `pins(conn, bases)` replaces characters.py's private reach-in); (2) `_browse`, `browse`, `character_rows`, `list_tags` to `tag_browse.py`; (3) `detail` plus `image_ids` to `tag_detail.py`, one small private function per panel section (`_months`, `_loras`, `_embeddings`, `_workflows`, `_related`) and a single `_visible_tag_rows()` fragment shared with `image_ids`; (4) character classification per the previous finding. Pure move first, no behaviour change; the existing test_tag_index.py/test_tags_page_integration.py pin it.
invariants_touched: Tag index owns invalidation

findings.title: Cover pins and focus (tag_meta, tag_focus) are written from five modules including the router
findings.problem: set_tag_thumbnail / clear_tag_thumbnail build a `sqlite_insert(t.tag_meta)` upsert, an image-carries-tag EXISTS and the `tag_index.invalidate()` call inside the router (a router doing SQL, and a call-site invalidate, which CLAUDE.md says to avoid). The same table is also touched by tag_rename (move), tag_migrations (rekey) and library_nesting (repoint), while its read side (`_pins`, `pin_key`) is in tag_index and its sibling table tag_focus is in tag_focus.py. There is no single owner for a tag's cover.
findings.proposal: Create `services/tag_covers.py` owning both tables: `pin_key`, `pins(conn, bases)`, `async set_pin(tag_key, names, image_id) -> bool` (does the carries-tag check, upsert and invalidate, returns False for the 404), `clear_pin(tag_key)`, `move(conn, old, new)` (today's `_move_thumbnail` focus+pin half), and the focus functions from tag_focus.py (`clean`, `put`, `get`, `all_focus`, `for_cover`). The two thumbnail routes shrink to validate, call, map to HTTP; the face_detect call stays in the router or characters.
invariants_touched: Invalidation is structural; routers don't reach for the cache

findings.title: PUT /tags/focus runs the full 8-query detail aggregate just to learn the pin and existence
findings.problem: `set_tag_focus` calls `tag_index.detail(base, 'all')` (months, loras, embeddings, workflows, related, characters) and uses only `got['thumb_image_id']` (the pin) and `is None` (existence). Each focus nudge in the picker pays the whole panel cost. `tag_detail` then recomputes the same cover with `_cover_of`.
findings.proposal: Add `tag_covers.cover_of(base) -> str | None` (pin if present and visible, else the mosaic lead via `samples_for_tag('any:'+base, 1)`; None when no visible image carries the base) and use it in set_tag_focus (404 when None) and tag_detail (which already has the pin from `detail`). Delete the router-level `_cover_of`.

findings.title: api/tags.py builds service-level caches and repeats a library-bases query
findings.problem: `_tag_maps`, `_library_bases`, `board_offers` and `place_tags` assemble derived caches (generation capture, `read_derived`/`store_derived`, `asyncio.to_thread`, a module-global asyncio.Lock) and run SQL in the router. `_tag_maps` and `_library_bases` both run `SELECT DISTINCT image_tags.base` and cache separately, so a tag write triggers the scan twice. The idiom `tag_index.pin_key(validate_tags([tag])[0])` appears 8 times.
findings.proposal: Move `library_bases()`, `tag_maps()` and `board_offers()` into a `services/tag_views.py` (they are derived views over the tag index with the same invalidation rule); `tag_maps` takes its `library` from `library_bases()`. In the router add one dependency `def _base(tag: str = Query(...)) -> str` returning `pin_key(validate_tags([tag])[0])` for character/detail/focus/thumbnail routes. Router keeps only HTTP mapping.

findings.title: Rule changes reproject synchronously in two of three paths while add_rules has a background threshold
findings.problem: `add_rules` reprojects inline up to 500 images, otherwise `reproject_ids_async`. `rename_tag` (prompt branch) and `delete_alias` always run `reproject_ids` inline via `anyio.to_thread`, with no cap and no activity task, so merging or deleting a rule on a tag used by tens of thousands of images holds the HTTP request (and the single SQLite writer in 500-id chunks) for minutes, then returns a count the UI treats as done. The three paths also differ on who invalidates the tag index (inline: caller; async: reproject).
findings.proposal: Extract `async def _apply(affected: list[str]) -> bool` in tag_rename.py: sorted ids, inline up to `_SYNC_REPROJECT` (then `tag_index.invalidate()`), else `reproject_ids_async`; returns `background`. Use it in rename_tag, add_rules and delete_alias, and add `background` to the rename/delete responses (frontend already reads it for add_rules).

findings.title: Split image_tags into a pure tag-kinds vocabulary and the writer; this removes the tag_index import cycle
findings.problem: image_tags.py mixes four layers: pure tag-kind vocabulary (prefixes, canonical_tag, any: expansion, tag_match_groups, excluded_prefixes, base_of), rating normalization, image-id variants/row_to_doc, and the transactional writers. tag_index imports image_tags only for prefix helpers and `not_quarantined`, which forces image_tags to import tag_index lazily inside `_dirty_tag_index` ('keeping the import local is what breaks the cycle'). The tag-weights work will add weight handling into `_persist_statements` and the bulk twin, both in the 621-line module.
findings.proposal: Extract `services/tag_kinds.py` (no DB imports): MANUAL_PREFIX/PROMPT_PREFIX/ANY_PREFIX, is_*/to_*/base_of, canonical_tag, any_variants/expand_search_tag/tag_match_groups, excluded_prefixes, recompute_flags, plus `not_quarantined` into a tiny `image_filters` or schema helper. tag_index and every reader import tag_kinds; image_tags imports tag_index at module scope and re-exports nothing (update ~25 callers, mechanical). Keep `normalize_rating`, writers and scalar setters in image_tags.
findings.depends_on: Do before adding prompt weights to _persist_statements
invariants_touched: image_tags is the only mutator of tags (stays true)

findings.title: GET /tags (non-merged) computes thumbnails and pins nothing reads
findings.problem: The frontend's only two callers are `useTagAggregate` (type `{_id, count}`, used by OverviewPage for `tags.length`) and the gallery autocomplete with `merge_sources=1`. The per-tag branch still selects `MAX(image_id)` as `sample_image_id`, queries `tag_meta` pins and returns `thumb_image_id` per tag; that value can be a quarantined image and nothing consumes it. It is an extra join plus a payload field per tag on a library with tens of thousands of tags.
findings.proposal: Drop `sample_image_id`, the `_pins` call and `thumb_image_id` from the non-merge branch of `list_tags` (return `{_id, count}`), update test_tags_integration.py expectations if they assert it. Optionally give Overview a dedicated count instead of the whole list.

findings.title: 'alias' names three different things; the user's merge rules are still called aliases in code and routes
findings.problem: CONTEXT.md calls the user's rewrites Merge/Split rules (`tag_rules`), but the code says `apply_aliases` (tag_names), `_load_aliases` (reproject), `list_aliases`/`delete_alias` (tag_rename), `/tags/aliases` routes, while `danbooru_tags.TagList.aliases`, `tag_descriptions.with_aliases` and `characters` 'aliases' (bare names) mean other things. Reproject also keeps its own sync `tag_rules` reader beside tag_rename._load_rules, and `apply_aliases` lives in tag_names though it is rule application, so weight-carrying merges will have to touch an oddly placed function.

Keep the `/aliases` URL for now (frontend contract) or alias it in the same pass. Leave Danbooru and character 'aliases' as they are.

results.health: The feed core is in good shape: FeedFilter validates on construction, the feed and grouped view share one WHERE builder, cursor shape lives in one SORTS table, and the frontend keeps filter/URL round-trip and layout math pure and tested. The weak spots are all at the edges. feed_where (radon F48) and _drive_by_rarest normalize tags and prompt terms separately, api/images.py is a four-job router whose route order is load-bearing, imageFilter.ts mixes codec, API client and search-term logic, and AllImagesPage is a 1338-line page that hand-rolls what hooks and queries already exist. The grouped (batch) view is a second-class citizen of the cache and polling layer, which is the one real bug cluster found.

findings.title: Grouped gallery view is not refreshed or patched: flat feed always fetches, poll refetches the wrong query, removals skip groups
findings.problem: useImageFeed(filters) has no `enabled` flag, so in grouped mode (persisted in localStorage, so the default for a user who likes batches) the page fetches both the hidden flat feed and the visible groups. The library poll then does `refetchFeedRef.current = feed.refetch`, i.e. it refetches the hidden flat feed, never `groups`, so a finished scan or watcher event does not update the grouped tiles the user is looking at. removeImagesFromFeeds goes through patchFeeds, which only walks the `images` prefix (feedQueries), so bulk quarantine from selection mode in grouped view, and a purge from ImageView, leave the tile in the groups cache until the later invalidateFeeds lands (bulk: after every request in runBulk finishes). imageFeedKey also embeds `group`, which /images ignores, so toggling Group refetches and splits the flat cache.
findings.proposal: Add `enabled` to useImageFeed and call `useImageFeed(filters, PAGE_LIMIT, !groupMode)`. Replace refetchFeedRef with `activeFeed.refetch`. In feedCache add `groupQueries` handling to patchFeeds (or a sibling `patchGroups`) so removeImagesFromFeeds drops ids from both caches. Build imageFeedKey from `{...filters, group: false}` so the flat cache is shared across the Group toggle. Add a feedCache vitest that removing an id also removes it from an ['image-groups'] query.
invariants_touched: useImageFeed: AllImagesPage and ImageView read one cache

findings.title: AllImagesPage (1338 lines) fuses polling, shortcuts, triage, bulk actions, filter option queries and the whole filter panel
findings.problem: One component owns eight jobs. The pure-ish ones have no tests because they are closures inside the page: the three-way workflow picker option building (244-271), the n/a/q toggle logic that also rewrites aiTagged (485-492), triage focus clamping (627-628), bulk quarantine/tag orchestration (699-778). The filter panel JSX alone is about 195 lines (1051-1246) and re-implements the same exclusivity rule inline in three onClicks (381, 394).
findings.proposal: Move in this order, each a pure move: (1) components/GalleryFilterPanel.tsx taking {filters,setFilters, options} for lines 1051-1246, with a hook `hooks/useFilterOptions.ts` returning tagOptions, model/lora/embedding options, outfits, resourceSuggestions, knownResources, workflowPickerOptions (198-271); (2) hooks/useGalleryShortcuts.ts for 443-510 and hooks/useTriage.ts for 590-690 (takes items, focusedIndex, filters, density); (3) hooks/useBulkActions.ts for 699-778 returning runBulkQuarantine/runBulkTag/runBulkManualTags; (4) components/GalleryToolbar.tsx for the header JSX 805-1003 (the desktop and phone variants of Sort/Group/Select currently duplicated, 891-959). Put the n/a/q toggles and workflow picker mapping in lib/ as pure functions with vitest. Page shrinks to roughly 300 lines of composition.

findings.title: feed_where (radon F48) and _drive_by_rarest each re-derive the same tag groups and prompt-term list
findings.problem: The canonical_tag + tag_match_groups step (205-206 vs 354-355) and the `[canonical_name(p.lower()) for p in pterms if p and p.strip()]` normalization (229 vs 358) are written twice. The driver is documented as 'every group is ANDed into the filter, so its images are a superset of the result', which only holds while the two copies agree, so a change to one (say a new tag alias rule, or pterms OR semantics) silently makes the driver prune real matches. `no_ai_tags` is also emitted in both arms of an if/else (209, 214). feed_where itself is one 125-line function with 38 branches mixing tags, gen terms, loras, outfits, sizes and workflow.
findings.proposal: Add two small pure helpers: `_tag_groups(f) -> list[list[str]]` and `_pterms(f) -> list[str]`, used by both feed_where and _drive_by_rarest. Then split feed_where into `_tag_conds(f)`, `_gen_conds(f)` (pterms, model, lora, embedding, workflow, needs_mapping), `_outfit_conds(f)` and `_size_conds(f)`, each returning list[ColumnElement]; feed_where becomes `sa.and_(*_tag_conds(f), *_gen_conds(f), ...)`. Hoist `no_ai_tags` out of the if/else. Cover with the existing test_image_feed/test_feed_integration plus one test asserting driver_ids never changes the result set.
invariants_touched: feed and grouped view share one builder
Tag names canonicalized at every entry

findings.title: imageFilter.ts mixes URL codec, API client and search-term logic; the gallery uses raw api() for tags, ids and a hand-rolled libraries poll
findings.problem: The file header calls parseFilters/serializeFilters 'pure', but 60 lines of it are fetch wrappers (fetchImagesPage, fetchGroupsPage, fetchImage, which RulesPage and ImageView also import from a filter module) and 80 lines are search-box term mapping (resourceOf, searchTerms, withSearchTerms). In the page, the merged tag-suggestion query, /images/ids and the libraries poll are inline `api(...)` calls. The page also reimplements useLibraries (queries.ts:76) by polling every 1.5s/8s, mirroring the result into useState AND setQueryData; the only extra is the watcher `last_event_at` detection.
findings.proposal: Split into lib/imageFilter.ts (types + codec + chips, pure), lib/imageApi.ts (fetchImagesPage, fetchGroupsPage, fetchImage, fetchImageIds, buildImagesQuery) and lib/searchTerms.ts (RESOURCE_PREFIXES through withSearchTerms, with its existing tests). Add to lib/queries.ts `tagSuggestionsQuery` (merge_sources), `imageSizesQuery` (move useSizePresets out of SizeFilter.tsx, which Generate also imports) and let the page call `useLibraries()` (drop `libs` useState) plus a `useFeedAutoRefresh(libs, refetch)` hook that holds only the scanning/last_event_at transition logic.

findings.title: Filter axes are hand-listed in eight places and the aiTagged exclusivity rule is re-applied by each
findings.problem: Adding a filter axis means touching the Filters type, DEFAULT_FILTERS, parse, serialize, hasActiveFilter, withoutFilters, activeFilterChips and the filter panel; hasActiveFilter and withoutFilters can already disagree (withoutFilters keeps libraryId/groupId, hasActiveFilter counts them). The rule 'aiTagged is ignored beside noTags/noAiTags' is applied in parse (144), serialize (183), chips (375), two hotkeys (487, 492) and two panel buttons, while the backend rejects the combination with 422, so a hand-built URL is silently repaired in the UI. The `workflow` vs `workflowSig` 'one or the other' comment (89-90) is not enforced anywhere on the client, but both are ANDed by the backend.
findings.proposal: Add `normalizeFilters(f): Filters` in imageFilter.ts that enforces aiTagged exclusivity and workflow/workflowSig exclusivity, call it at the end of parseFilters and inside useFilters.setFilters, and delete the per-call-site repairs. Define hasActiveFilter as 'serializeFilters(withoutView(f)) has params' where withoutView drops logic/sort/group/libraryId, so a new axis is picked up by the codec alone. Test: one table-driven vitest that every Filters key round-trips and that a new key without a serialize line fails.

findings.title: api/images.py is four routers in one file and its route order is load-bearing; original-file GET/HEAD repeat path resolution
findings.problem: One 644-line router holds the feed (list, ids, groups), media delivery (file/thumb/thumb-url with GET+HEAD, ETag, small-copy limiter), facet lists (models/loras/embeddings/sizes), activity stats, and curation writes (rating/score/quarantine/purge). The fixed paths (/ids, /models, /loras, /embeddings, /sizes, /stats, /groups) only work because they are declared before the `/{image_id:path}` catch-alls; a new route added at the bottom of the file is silently swallowed as an image id. get_image_file and head_image_file (156-209) repeat the lookup, path check, isfile check and mimetype guess.
findings.proposal: Create api/image_media.py (file/thumb/head/thumb-url plus `_original_path(image_id)` shared by GET and HEAD), api/image_facets.py (models, loras, embeddings, sizes, stats), keep feed + curation in images.py. In main.py mount the facets and feed router first and the media/curation routers (which own `/{image_id:path}/...`) last, with a comment and a test that GET /images/stats and /images/sizes are not captured by the catch-all. purge_image should delete the DB rows before unlinking the file so a failed transaction cannot leave a row whose file is gone.
invariants_touched: New media endpoints serve from the FS with a HEAD counterpart

findings.title: Model, LoRA and embedding filter counts include quarantined images, Size counts do not; three facet routes are near-copies
findings.problem: CONTEXT.md says counts leave quarantined images out so a count matches its gallery link. /sizes does (`.where(image_tags.not_quarantined())`), but /models, /loras and /embeddings do not, so a dropdown showing 'NahidaXL 120' opens a gallery of fewer images when some are quarantined. The three routes also differ for no reason: loras uses count() while embeddings uses count(distinct image_id), and library scoping is a join in two and a where in the other two.
findings.proposal: One helper `_facet_base(library_id)` returning `select(...).where(not_quarantined())` joined to images when scoped, used by all four routes; use count(distinct image_id) uniformly for the join-table facets. Add an integration test that quarantining an image lowers the model/lora/embedding counts.

findings.title: useFilters reads and writes localStorage unguarded, unlike every sibling view-pref hook
findings.problem: useFilters calls localStorage.getItem inside a useMemo during render and setItem on every setFilters, with no try/catch. In a private window or with site data blocked the accessor can throw, which takes down the whole gallery page (and every filter change). useDensity and useScrollRestoration both wrap the same access. findings.title: Per-tile preResolved/resolveMediaUrl branch in the load slot is dead for the gallery; density clamp written four times

Export `clampDensity(d)` from masonryLayout.ts and use it in all four places.

Extract the crossfade effect into hooks/useCrossfade.ts returning {layers, front} from a `src` string, and test its sequence (set, swap, clear after SCRUB_CROSSFADE_MS) with fake timers.

results.health: The scan, watch and thumbnail stack is carefully commented and well covered (blurhash, storage_fs, scan_writer, nesting and discover are small, deep, testable modules). The weak points are structural: api/libraries.py holds the whole library lifecycle (and api/generate.py calls its handlers directly), image-row deletion is copy-pasted five times, scanner.py (898 lines) fuses five jobs, and the frontend spreads library writes and scan polling across four files with inconsistent cache invalidation. Already reported and not repeated: the _run closure, event-loop blocking joins, unbounded stale-delete transactions, dead file_hash, scan_error never shown in the UI.

findings.title: Library lifecycle lives in api/libraries.py and is reused by calling route handlers from another router
findings.problem: add/move/remove are ordered sequences of side effects (DB write, library_nesting.invalidate, tag_index.invalidate, cancel_scan, start/stop_watch, scan_library_async, _rescan_libraries_around, delete_by_prefix) written inline in three route handlers. api/generate.py put_comfyui imports and awaits add_library and update_library as plain functions (and wraps them in `except ValueError`, which they never raise: they raise HTTPException), so the sequence is already a service with no service module. Consequences visible today: remove_library never deletes the `thumbs:{library_id}` stamp row scanner._save_stamp writes (orphaned forever); the event-loop-blocking joins (already reported) have to be fixed in three places; add_library has a check-then-insert race (two concurrent POSTs for one path both pass the dedupe, the second hits the primary key and returns 500); library_id_for and _rescan_libraries_around are router-private helpers.
findings.proposal: Add services/library_ops.py with async `create(path, name, watch)`, `move_or_edit(id, patch)`, `remove(id)`, `rescan_around(path, exclude)` and `library_id_for`. Each owns its full side-effect order, runs the cancel/join/start_watch calls via anyio.to_thread, deletes the scanner stamp row on remove, and makes create idempotent on IntegrityError (return the existing row). Routes become validate, call, shape response. api/generate.py put_comfyui calls `library_ops.ensure_watched(path, name)` instead of the two handlers. Return one response shape from create (existing rows return the full row, new ones a 3-key dict today).

findings.title: Image-row deletion (rows, raw gen, thumbnails, tag index) is hand-written in five places
findings.problem: Every site does `delete(images)` + `delete(image_gen_raw)` in the same transaction, then tag_index.invalidate(), then best-effort delete_thumb per key, each with its own lazy `from .storage_fs import delete_thumb` inside try/except pass (scanner.py:325 and :801 import lazily although put_thumb is already imported at module top, so there is no cycle to avoid). A sixth table that must cascade (the next derived table, or tag weights if stored beside the image) has to be added in five places; the scanner and nesting variants also forget to refresh libraries.indexed_count consistently (nesting recounts, remove_single_image uses a delta, the scan sets it from the walk).
findings.proposal: New small module (e.g. services/image_delete.py): `delete_rows(conn, ids) -> list[thumb_key]` (sync) plus an async twin used by purge/remove_library, and `drop_thumbs(keys)` (best-effort, logs at debug). Callers keep ownership of the transaction and call `tag_index.invalidate()` after commit, but the table list and the thumb cleanup exist once. The unbounded-transaction fix already reported for the scanner stale delete then lands in one chunking loop (200 ids per tx) used by scanner, nesting and remove_library.

findings.title: scanner.py (898 lines) fuses thumbnail rendering, scan stamp, reconcile policy, watcher entry points and the scan thread
findings.problem: One module owns five jobs with different consumers: (1) thumbnail recipe (_THUMB_*, thumb_stamp, _make_thumb_bytes, is_image) which library_discover imports from the scanner, pulling PIL, gen_metadata and the whole scan machinery into a dry-run path counter; (2) the stamp/retry persistence (_load_stamp/_save_stamp); (3) the pure reconcile policy (reconcile_stale, stale_guard, unread_prefixes), the highest-risk code in the file; (4) the watcher-facing incremental API (ingest_single_file, remove_single_image, _touch_library); (5) the scan thread, slots and cancel registry. The cancel/slot state (_scan_lock, _current_scans, _cancel_scans, _scan_threads, _scans_ended) is module globals reached via scans_ended/is_scanning/cancel_scan.
findings.proposal: Split along existing seams, keeping `scanner` as the public facade so no caller changes: `thumbnailer.py` (recipe constants, thumb_stamp, make_thumb_bytes, is_image; library_discover imports this), `scan_reconcile.py` (reconcile_stale, stale_guard, unread_prefixes, plus the stamp load/save), `incremental.py` (ingest_single_file, remove_single_image, _touch_library, used only by library_watch), and scanner.py keeps the thread/slot/cancel registry and the (already flagged) _run, which can then shrink to orchestration. Pure moves, tests keep importing through `scanner` re-exports for one release.

findings.title: LibrariesPage runs its own raw-fetch progress poller beside useLibraries, which already polls the same fields
findings.problem: GET /libraries (polled every 3 s by useLibraries while anything scans) already returns scanning, scan_total, scan_done, indexed_count. LibrariesPage additionally keeps a `progress` state, a prevScanningRef, and a 1.5 s setTimeout loop that does a raw `fetch('/api/v1/libraries/${id}/progress')` per scanning library (bypassing lib/api and TanStack), only to detect the scanning to done edge and invalidate the feed. Two sources of truth for 'is it scanning' (`progress[id]?.scanning || l.scanning`) can disagree for a poll tick, and WelcomePage ScanProgress is a third poller of the same list. The page is also 717 lines: card, edit dialog, selection state and folder-collapse persistence all inline.
findings.proposal: Delete the progress state and effect; render the bar from the library row (`scan_done/scan_total`). Detect the scanning to done edge in useLibraries itself (a small effect or select comparing the previous list) and invalidate the image feeds there. Keep GET /libraries/{id}/progress only because tests/perf_benchmark.py uses it, or switch the benchmark to the list endpoint and delete the route. Then split the page: `LibraryCard.tsx`, `EditLibraryDialog.tsx`, `hooks/useLibrarySelection.ts`, and a `useCollapsedFolders` hook (the same localStorage-set pattern exists elsewhere).

findings.title: Frontend library writes (create, edit, delete, rescan) are spread over four files with inconsistent cache invalidation
findings.problem: The same REST calls are made with raw `api(...)` and hand-built JSON headers from LibrariesPage (PATCH, DELETE x2, POST rescan), AddLibraryDialog (POST loop with per-row failure collection), WelcomePage.createLibraries (DELETE + POST loop with per-row failure collection, near-identical to the dialog's), and libraryPlan (discover). Only LibrariesPage invalidates the image feeds (`['images']`, `['image-groups']`) after a change; WelcomePage and AddLibraryDialog's callers rely on the page to do it, so creating or removing libraries from setup leaves a cached gallery stale. The two 'which candidates become libraries' rules also differ silently (defaultSelected: new and not hidden; onboarding.librariesToAdd/sourceTotals: new or empty and not hidden).
findings.proposal: Add lib/libraryApi.ts: `createLibraries(items) -> {created: Map<path,id>, failed: string[]}` (shared by dialog and setup), `updateLibrary`, `deleteLibrary`, `rescanLibrary`, and a `useLibraryMutations()` hook that owns `invalidate(LIBRARIES_KEY, ['images'], ['image-groups'])` so every caller gets the same cache behaviour. Move the candidate-eligibility predicates (`isAddable`, `defaultSelected`, the onboarding variant) into libraryPlan.ts beside the types with one comment on why empty folders differ.

findings.title: Folder ancestry and 'innermost library' are implemented four ways
findings.problem: library_nesting owns the rule (path_key + is_inside, case-folded where the OS is). library_discover re-derives it with os.path.commonpath on un-case-folded strings (_is_within), so a Windows library stored as `D:/Images` and a candidate `d:/images/x` are judged by different rules in the dry run and in the scan. generation_jobs.held_by re-implements 'innermost library holding this file' as its own best-length loop, and library_nesting._adopt_from does the same with max(holders, key=len). library_discover also re-exports normalize_path through `__all__` only so api/libraries.py can call `library_discover.normalize_path` (twice) instead of importing it from models.library. The frontend has a fourth spelling in normalizeLibraryPath (display grouping only, acceptable).
findings.proposal: Add `library_nesting.innermost(path, libraries) -> (id, root) | None` and use it in _adopt_from and generation_jobs.held_by. Make library_discover._classify use `path_key`/`is_inside` (and a `related(a, b)` helper) instead of _is_within. Drop normalize_path from library_discover.__all__ and import it from models.library in the router. One test table of path pairs (posix, drive letters, case) shared by discover and nesting tests.

findings.title: Moving a library while it is scanning leaves the scan on the old folder and nothing rescans
findings.problem: update_library on a path change calls scan_library_async(library_id, new_path), which returns {'started': False, 'status': 'already_running'} when a scan is in flight (the result is ignored). The running scan only re-reads libraries.path once, right after it gets its slot (scanner.py:588-594), so a scan already walking continues on the old root, writes rows with old absolute paths, and its stale reconciliation runs against that old root. The new location is not scanned until the watcher's reconcile timer fires (and never if watch_enabled is false). The same ignored return value applies to every caller of scan_library_async in the router.
findings.proposal: In the move path (in library_ops.move, see finding 1) call cancel_scan via to_thread, wait for it to end (join with a longer timeout than the 0.5 s default), then start the scan; or have scan_library_async record a `rescan_requested` flag that _run checks in its finally block and re-enters once. Add an integration test: start a scan, PATCH path, assert the final rows carry the new root.

findings.title: What counts as an indexable file is decided in three places and the rules disagree
findings.problem: The full scan walks every file and keeps anything with an IMAGE_EXTS suffix or any mimetype that starts with image/ (so .svg, .tif, .ico, and whatever the host mime table adds). The watcher additionally drops dotfiles, ~files and .tmp/.part suffixes, but the scan does not, so `.cover.png` is indexed by a scan yet its watcher delete event is ignored and the row lingers until the next reconcile. A file Pillow cannot open (an .svg) passes is_image, _make_thumb_bytes returns (None, None, 0, 0, None) from a swallowed exception, and _process_image still returns ok=True with width=0, height=0 and thumb_key=None: it is indexed as a blank tile, never counted in failed_count, never listed in the retry ids, and rebuilt on every rescan because _unchanged needs a thumb_key. The discover preview counts with is_image only, so its numbers differ from both.
findings.proposal: One predicate `is_indexable(path)` in the new thumbnailer/scan module (extension allow-list, no generic mimetype fallback unless intended, plus the ignore rules) used by the walk, the watcher, ingest and library_discover._count_images. Treat a decode failure (width == 0) as a failed result (ok False, stage 'decode') so it appears in scan_failed_samples and the retry list instead of a silent blank row. Low confidence the mimetype fallback is accidental: confirm with the author before narrowing it.

findings.title: Thumbnail key is built by two formulas, and the thumb_format setting is half implemented
findings.problem: put_thumb builds `f'{library_id}/{image_id}.webp'.replace(':','_')` from its two arguments while thumb_key(image_id) rebuilds the same string by splitting the id on ':'. thumb_version.urls() and urls_for_rows() trust the derived form (urls ignores the stored thumb_key entirely), so a URL is only correct while the two formulas agree; the put_thumb docstring claims readers need 'no matching transform', which is false. Separately, settings.thumb_format lets the scanner encode JPEG or PNG bytes but the key always ends `.webp` and the small copy is always WEBP, so a non-webp setting stores mislabelled files (it works only because browsers sniff content).
findings.proposal: Make put_thumb call thumb_key(image_id) (assert the library prefix matches) so there is one formula, and fix the docstring. Either remove thumb_format and the convert branch in _make_thumb_bytes (and from thumb_stamp), or derive the suffix from it in the one key function. Prefer removal: nothing in the UI sets it and CLAUDE.md describes WebP thumbnails.

findings.title: library_watch.py mixes a child-process supervisor with per-library event routing; _write_loop is radon D21
findings.problem: Lines 134-304 (_writer, _send, _add_cmd, _write_loop, _write, _close, _spawn, _back_off, _read_child, restart backoff globals) are a generic 'keep a JSON-lines child alive, replay its adds on respawn, drop commands while it is down' supervisor with no knowledge of libraries beyond `_watches`, which it reads unlocked and under `_lock` in different places. The rest is library semantics (_Watch, _run_watch debounce-merge, _wait_stable, reconcile timer, start/stop). The supervisor's tricky state machine (readded set, closing event, want_child, per-writer queue retired by stop_all) can only be tested through real subprocesses (test_library_watch_proc.py).
findings.proposal: Extract `services/watch_child.py` with `class ChildWatcher(on_message, current_adds)` exposing `add(cmd)`, `remove(key)`, `close(timeout)`; spawn and clock injectable. library_watch keeps _Watch, routing (`on_message` = _route) and the reconcile timer and passes `lambda: [_add_cmd(w) for w in _watches.values()]` as the respawn replay source. Gives _write_loop a unit-test surface with a fake process.

findings.title: Character signature pipeline is written twice and recomputed uncached on every outfit request and image view
findings.problem: recipes._signature and characters.page both do the same read: count the character's images, count visible images, signature_counts, signature(visible=vocab.general, skip=...), with different limits and then different filters (facet_of in LOOK vs is_identity/is_attire). The visible-image count query is written three times (characters.py:634, recipes.py:259, recipes.py:363, the last two inside one recipe() call). Worse, every outfit entry point goes through recipes.wardrobe, which recomputes the whole signature with no cache: outfits.default, covers, prefill, update_default (twice), and worn() once per character in the image (up to 10), on every image view with characters (WornOutfits). Each call also repeats characters._named (tag_index.browse plus vocab load) two to three times (_key -> character_key, then default -> wardrobe -> character_key). characters.create runs _named twice and update -> names_of a third time. tag_index already has a generation-keyed store (read_derived/store_derived) that exists for exactly this, structurally invalidated by tag writes.
findings.proposal: Add one function in characters.py (or a new character_look module), e.g. `async def look_of(key, names, key_of, rows) -> Look(n, counted, sig_tags, gender, hair_eyes_rows)`, holding the n/total/signature_counts/signature steps, and have both characters.page and recipes._signature call it. Add `tag_index.visible_count(conn)` for the three duplicate count queries. Memoize look_of (and recipes.wardrobe) per key with tag_index.read_derived/store_derived using the generation captured before computing, so no call site invalidates. Let outfits.worn resolve all keys with one _named call (pass the resolved key into default(), skipping the second character_key). Keep the public signatures; tests in test_recipes/test_outfits/test_characters stay valid.

findings.title: characters.page computes the character-only look for every plain tag page
findings.problem: /tags/:tag reuses characters.page for any tag (api/tags.py says 'Any other tag gets the same page'). page() has no branch on detail['category']: for a plain tag like 'smile' it still runs signature_counts (a count over every image of the tag), the hair/eye query, the signature with attire.facet_of filtering, and solo_palette. The frontend ignores signature, signature_images and palette when person is false (Profile only reads signature if person, colours only if person). page is radon D(23) because it fuses the tag-page core (detail, cover, with, best, scored, ratings, lora scores) with the character-only look. Cost scales with the tag's image count, so the biggest plain tags are the slowest pages.

Call _page_look only when detail['category'] == 'character' or meta kind == 'character'; otherwise return palette [], signature [], signature_images 0 so the response shape the frontend types expect stays unchanged. Name the plain-tag use in the docstring or move the plain-tag branch to a small tag_page wrapper, since the module is the Character page owner per CONTEXT.md.

findings.title: Deleting a hand-made character leaves its outfits, Default edits and hides behind
findings.problem: remove_made deletes characters, recipe_edits, recipe_additions and recipe_genders rows, but not the character's rows in outfits (character column), outfit_defaults (character) or outfit_hidden (character), nor a tag_meta pin. Their private outfits stay in the Outfits page list (outfits.listing() with no character returns every row), where they have no character: the card falls back to the raw tag, editing opens SaveOutfitDialog whose cover grid and prefill 404 because recipes.wardrobe returns None, and a shared outfit from the deleted character stays in everyone's list with a dangling owner. The confirm text only promises 'Their identity tags and LoRA go too'. Re-creating a character with the same tag later silently resurrects the old outfits.
findings.proposal: In remove_made, in the same async_tx, also delete t.outfits where character == tag (and their outfit_hidden rows by outfit_id), t.outfit_hidden where character == tag, and t.outfit_defaults where character == tag. Decide for shared outfits (keep with the owner cleared, or delete); simplest is delete all, and say so in the confirm message ('Their outfits go too'). Add a test next to test_made_character_can_be_deleted that saves an outfit first.

findings.title: promptOutline (board) and prompt_parse (tags) read the same prompt differently; an unclosed bracket makes the board see one term
findings.problem: Both sides are meant to produce the same term names (the board matches its terms to the backend's prompt tags via /tags/place and the prompt: tags). Verified differences: (1) FE splitSpans does depth++ on every '(' / '[' and only splits at depth 0, so one unclosed '(' (or the emoticon ';(' / '>:(' that the backend knows whole) swallows every later comma into one piece; backend _scan always cuts at separators whatever the stack holds. (2) Backend also splits on '|', BREAK and AND and treats '{}' as a group and emoticons (:d, ^_^, ;)) as whole tags; FE knows none of these. (3) FE prose = 5+ words with no underscore; backend is_prose needs 9+ words, or 5+ with a sentence end or a pronoun/article/verb marker, so a 5-word spaced tag is 'prose' on the board and a tag in the DB. (4) Backend strips a bare decimal weight ('smile:1.05') and edge punctuation ('smile.'); FE keeps both in the name (the test at promptOutline.test.ts:49 pins the colon case), so the board term name differs from the stored tag. (5) Weight rule: neither side computes it (already reported), so this is the same gap seen from the name side.
findings.proposal: Put one table of cases in packages/backend/tests/fixtures/prompt_terms.json: {text, terms:[{name, kind, weight?}]}. Read it from test_prompt_parse.py (parse_prompt -> names/kinds) and from a promptOutline vitest. Start by listing today's disagreements as the expected output, decide per row which side is right (backend is the one that writes tags, so default to backend), then make promptOutline.splitSpans cut at separators regardless of depth, add '|'/BREAK/AND and the emoticon whole-token rule, and replace PROSE_WORDS with a port of is_prose (or serve it). Merge with the existing 'prompt weight' fixture proposed in docs/tag-weights-plan.md so there is one fixture file with names, kinds and weights. Longer term, expose a POST /tags/parse-prompt and let the board call it instead of a second parser.

findings.problem: _runner catches every Exception and stores it on the state (status 'error', error text), so awaiting the task in wait() returns normally. download_wd_tagger then returns the expected paths without checking the state, and WDTagger.load goes straight to _load_labels_from_csv, which raises FileNotFoundError ('No such file or directory ...csv'). findings.title: AI worker loop dies on any error outside the per-image try, leaving the job 'running' and every later job queued forever
findings.problem: _worker_loop sets job.status='running' and then runs get_ai_settings() (a DB read), set_idle_unload_s and resolved_model_target outside any except. Add a test that makes get_ai_settings raise for one job and checks a second job still completes.

findings.title: Library scan state is polled four independent ways, including a hand-rolled fetch loop that duplicates fields the list already carries
findings.problem: useLibraries already polls LIBRARIES_KEY every 3s while any library is scanning, and Library already carries scan_total and scan_done. Yet LibrariesPage runs a second useEffect+setTimeout loop that raw-fetches /libraries/{id}/progress per scanning library every 1.5s into a local `progress` state, and does its own scanning->done transition detection (prevScanningRef) to refresh and invalidate the feed. AllImagesPage runs a third loop (api('/libraries'), local setLibs, plus queryClient.setQueryData(LIBRARIES_KEY) to push into the cache) with its own wasScanningRef and lastEventSeenRef transition logic to refetch the feed. WelcomePage's ScanProgress runs a fourth useQuery on the same key with its own 2s interval and a separate queryFn instance. useBackgroundTasks has a fifth notion of 'scan ended' that invalidates libraries and tags. Two loops write the same cache key at different cadences, the transition detectors can disagree, and the only fetch that bypasses the cache (LibrariesPage progress) swallows every error silently.
findings.proposal: Make queries.ts the single owner. Keep useLibraries as the only poller (optionally let callers pass a faster interval via an option rather than a second useQuery). Add `useLibraryScanEvents({ onSettled })` (or fold into useLibraries) that diffs previous vs next data once and calls back on scanning->done and on a changed last_event_at; export a pure `scanTransitions(prev, next)` in lib/ with a test. Then LibrariesPage drops `progress` state and reads l.scan_done/l.scan_total, AllImagesPage replaces its tick() with the callback (`feed.refetch` + nothing else), and WelcomePage reuses useLibraries. Delete the per-library /progress fetch call site (and the endpoint if nothing else uses it).

findings.title: Error toasts show raw JSON in ~25 places: three different error-to-text styles, errorText used only for onboarding/library flows

findings.title: JsonTree branch toggle opens and closes every sibling branch at once
findings.problem: Each JsonTree instance holds one `open` state (initially depth < 2) but renders many child entries. The per-child expand button calls `setOpen(o => !o)` on the parent instance, and every child computes `childOpen = open || ...` from that same state. So at depth 0 (where the root is open) clicking one node's arrow collapses all nodes; below depth 2 (closed by default) clicking one arrow expands every sibling branch of that node at once. The pin-a-path UI on Rules and the guessed-prompt marks therefore feel erratic on large graphs; the existing tests only cover path construction and search reveal, not manual toggling.
findings.proposal: Move the toggle state to the child: extract a small `Branch` component (key, value, path) that owns its own `useState(depth < 2)` and renders the button plus the nested JsonTree; JsonTree maps entries to either a leaf row or a Branch. Keep `open || matches || marks` as the forced-open rule inside Branch. Add a vitest that clicks one arrow and asserts siblings stay as they were.

findings.title: Setup payload computes fields nothing reads, and the page's checklist re-derives the server's checks

Either way delete `_consumers`, `found.lora.consumers` and `found.lora.existing` (the separate found.loras list already serves the UI) and their test assertions (test_generator_discovery.py:59). findings.problem: ComfyStep.read and RulesPage.importFiles both do: filter .json, parseWorkflowFile each, count the skipped, call importWorkflowFiles. Rewrite the two fetches with api()/errorText. Optionally move the two network functions to lib/workflowQueries.ts so workflows.ts stays pure.

findings.title: lora_stem is a model-name rule living in the graph module; workflow.ts / workflows.ts / WorkflowFamily names collide
findings.problem: lora_stem is the key matching ComfyUI files to image_loras.name, used by comfy_models, remix, recipes and lora_presets (4 non-graph modules), and comfy_models even applies it to checkpoints and embeddings (stem=lora_stem(n) for kind 'checkpoint'/'embedding'). findings.title: discover() is one 90-line function (radon D27) mixing six slot readers; text_inputs and check_slots are D21 and D23

findings.title: Gallery and image URLs are hand-built in a dozen places instead of through lib/imageFilter
findings.problem: CLAUDE.md makes lib/imageFilter.ts the one filter/URL mapping, yet galleryHref(patch) is defined three times (search.ts, TagPanel.tsx, CharacterPage.tsx; the search.ts copy differs, returning '/' for an empty query where the others return '/?'). libraryGalleryHref in queries.ts is a fourth variant. ToReview and TagsPage hard-code '/?no_ai_tags=1', '/?no_tags=1', '/?quarantined=1', so renaming a filter param breaks them silently. findings.proposal: Add to lib/imageFilter.ts: `galleryHref(patch: Partial<Filters>): string` (DEFAULT_FILTERS merged, '/' when empty) and `imageHref(id: string, filters?: Filters): string`. Delete the three local galleryHref copies, make libraryGalleryHref call galleryHref({libraryId}), and have ToReview/TagsPage pass {noAiTags:true} etc. Add tests next to imageFilter.test.ts.

findings.title: Escape inside a Picker or DropdownMenu in a Dialog closes the whole Dialog
findings.problem: Dialog registers a capture-phase document keydown that handles Escape unconditionally (stopPropagation, onClose) for the topmost dialog. Picker handles Escape in a React onKeyDown and DropdownMenu in a bubble-phase document listener, both of which run after the Dialog's capture handler. So with a Picker open inside NewCharacterDialog (and generate/StyleLayer, Layers, CharacterBlock, LibrariesPage dialogs), Escape discards the dialog and any typed state rather than just closing the list. Tooltip's Escape has no stopPropagation either. Same class as the ImageView Escape bug in bugs.md, rooted in the primitives having no shared ownership of Escape.
findings.proposal: Introduce lib/overlayStack.ts (push/pop token, isTopmost) that Dialog, Picker, DropdownMenu, SearchPalette and Tooltip register with while open, so only the topmost overlay reacts to Escape/Tab. Minimal fix first: in Dialog's onKey, skip Escape when the event target is inside an element with aria-expanded='true' (the Picker/Dropdown trigger or its list) or when e.defaultPrevented. Add a Picker.test case for Escape inside a Dialog.
invariants_touched: No native browser menus: use Picker/DropdownMenu

findings.title: Sidebar defines NavButton as a component inside render, remounting every link on each shell render

Sidebar re-renders on every App state change (collapse toggle, mobile drawer, search open/close, route change), so a keyboard user who activates a nav link loses focus position, and hover/active transitions restart.

findings.title: Dead backend pieces and stale Mongo-era docs: models/image.py, models.library.Library, Settings.ai_tagging_url, db.write_lock()/sync_write_lock()
findings.problem: grep over src and tests finds no use of Image or ImageQuery (the whole of models/image.py), of models.library.Library, of settings.ai_tagging_url, or of the write_lock()/sync_write_lock() accessor functions (the underscored locks are used by async_tx/sync_tx). db.py's module docstring still says it 'Replaces the old Mongo motor.py' and points readers at the unused accessors, schema.py says pagination 'must match Mongo's byte-order sort', and the app_settings comment says 'currently only the "ai" row' when onboarding, migrations, tag settings, comfy settings, extraction settings and prompt presets all use it.
findings.proposal: Delete models/image.py, the Library class, ai_tagging_url, and the two accessor functions (and their __all__ entries); rewrite the three docstrings to describe current behaviour (SQLite byte order; app_settings holds many named rows). Keep ensure_schema_sync (used by tests/test_schema.py).

findings.title: main.py mixes wiring, a BaseHTTPMiddleware on every request, an in-memory rate limiter and the startup sequence
findings.problem: `@app.middleware('http')` is Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware, which wraps every response, thumbnails and originals included, in a streaming adapter; the project already wrote a pure-ASGI GZipExceptMedia precisely because media routes must pass through untouched, so the timing middleware undercuts that intent. The 'slow request' log stops at response headers (call_next returns when the response starts), so a slow FileResponse body is never counted. The rate limiter is off by default, covers one route (POST /libraries/*/rescan), and its _rl_state dict grows per client IP without eviction. vulture's 'unused _timing_and_rate_limit' is a false positive (decorator registration). The lifespan holds five unrelated startup steps inline.
findings.proposal: Move middleware to core/middleware.py: a pure-ASGI SlowRequestLog (timing around the whole send) next to GZipExceptMedia, and make the rescan limiter a small dependency on that one route with a bounded dict, or drop it if unused. Split lifespan into services/startup.py (run_startup_tasks: schema, migrations, nesting, thumb root, AI worker, watchers, generation) so main.py is only app assembly.

findings.title: SettingsContext is the AI-tagging controller under a generic name, and wraps every settings tab

SettingsPage mounts SettingsProvider for all sections, so opening the ComfyUI or Boilerplate tab still fetches AI settings and polls AI status. formatBytes (a generic formatter) lives in this file and is imported by two section files. Either render group titles in the tab strip or flatten SETTINGS_GROUPS into one list and fix the registry comment.
